podcast.title: Business Failure in 2001
podcast.body: The Beastie Boys' record label, Grand Royal, ultimately "ran up to many debts and went out of business in 2001." "The biggest exception was the band's record label, Grand Royal. It ran up to many debts and went out of business in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artist-Founded Label
podcast.body: Grand Royal was a private label established by the Beastie Boys themselves, using profits from "License to Ill," through which they signed other acts like Luscious Jackson. "The Beastie Boys moved to LA. They set up their own label called Grand Royal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Beastie Boys' Own Label
podcast.body: Grand Royal was the Beastie Boys' private record label, which they established after moving to Los Angeles, using profits from *License to Ill*. "They set up their own label called Grand Royal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Beyond Music - Magazine and Mailing List
podcast.body: As part of the expanding "Beastie Empire," Grand Royal diversified beyond just a record label, also launching its own magazine and a mailing list for fans. "Grand Royal also started a magazine and a mailing list."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Business Failure and Closure
podcast.body: The label eventually accumulated too many debts and went out of business in 2001, marking a significant exception to the otherwise successful "Beastie Empire." "The biggest exception was the band's record label, Grand Royal. It ran up to many debts, and went out of business in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Expansion Beyond Music
podcast.body: In addition to releasing music, Grand Royal expanded into other ventures, including starting "a magazine and a mailing list," diversifying the Beastie Boys' media presence. "Grand Royal also started a magazine and a mailing list."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
